messages.subject: Re: Never received ORDER L-39065
messages.text:
Hi Sonja,

Great question, and it's great to hear you already have a milkweed plant coming in.

Milkweed seeds planted in mid-summer can still germinate and grow this season, but they likely won't bloom until next year since milkweed is a perennial that usually flowers in its second year. Even young plants can help though, since the foliage itself is what monarch caterpillars feed on, so it's not too late to make a positive contribution this year.

When the seeds arrive, go ahead and plant them. They'll establish roots this season and come back stronger next year. You can also start them in small pots first to give them a head start before transplanting.

On that note, I owe you an apology. Your order has been waiting far too long, and that's simply not the kind of experience we want to give. This has been an intense stretch for us with real staffing challenges, but that's on us to fix, not something you should have to chase. I'm making sure your seeds go out right away, and I'll send you the tracking as soon as they're on their way.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
